function: Joint learned task offloading, satellite and beam selection, and uplink transmit power control for NOMA multi-beam LEO links, minimizing task completion latency (p. 6).
system: Single-antenna ground users, 4 LEO satellites at 550 km with 19 spot beams each, uplink NOMA, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 9).
method: Multi-agent hybrid PPO (MAHPPO): discrete and Gaussian sub-actors with centralized critic (CTDE); reinforcement learning trained offline in simulation, executed distributedly (p. 7).
data_channel: Custom UE5-based simulator; ITU-R S.465/S.1528 antenna gains, fading from unspecified path loss and small-scale model; no 3GPP model, public dataset, or measurements (p. 4, 5, 9).
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in the same simulated system; latency evaluated over 100 time slots while sweeping users, reuse factor K, and bandwidth; no unseen-condition test stated (p. 9-12).
baselines: Learned: MADDPG, QMIX, MAHPPO without action mask. Non-learned: random offloading; heuristic offloading to the largest-gain beam with average power (p. 10).
metrics: Average task completion latency (Figs. 9-13), training reward convergence, execution time per agent, and peak memory usage (p. 10-12).
complexity: Execution time per agent and peak memory: MAHPPO 0.785 ms, 2.440 KB; MADDPG 0.195 ms, 3.481 KB; QMIX 0.368 ms, 0.863 KB (Table I, p. 11).
q1_support: p. 5: "determined by path loss and small-scale fading" - no standardized channel model is named; only the antenna gains follow ITU-R S.465 and S.1528 (p. 4); the simulator is built in UE5 (p. 9); no measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "The average task completion latency under different numbers of users is shown in Fig. 9" - only sweeps of users, K and bandwidth; no policy trained in one condition and tested in another is stated, and p. 7: "training only needs to be re-conducted occasionally" when the environment changes.
q3_support: p. 10: "(MADDPG) and QMIX are used as benchmark algorithms" and "we consider the random offloading and heuristic offloading"; p. 10-11: latency in Figs. 9-10 is lower for MAHPPO than for all of them.
q4_support: p. 11: "MAHPPO exhibits the highest computational overhead, with an execution time of 0.785 ms and peak memory usage of 2.440 KB" (Table I also lists MADDPG and QMIX).
q5_support: p. 9: "used the open-source game engine Unreal Engine 5 (UE5)" to build its own simulator; no link to code or data, no public channel dataset, no measured data.
notes: Included under the clause that a work learning a physical-layer decision jointly with one above it passes above_phy: the learned action holds task offloading, beam selection and power control (p. 6), so area 6 (power and beam control of satellite links). q1=0 because ITU-R S.465/S.1528 give only antenna patterns (p. 4) and the fading model is unspecified; the reviewer may confirm. q2=0 because the sweeps of users, K and bandwidth (p. 10-12) are not stated as tests of a model trained elsewhere. q3=1 because MADDPG and QMIX are standard learning algorithms on the same problem, with latency compared; the ablation without action mask was not counted. q4=1 from the measured execution time and memory of Table I (p. 11). q5=0: own UE5 simulator, no release.
